correctness.rationale: Inclusion-exclusion gives the stated strict negative off-diagonal covariance. For one draw, \(C=\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T}\) has kernel exactly the constants. For \(n\ge2\), a zero covariance quadratic form makes \(\sum_i a_iI_i\) constant; singleton occupancy patterns force all coefficients equal, and positive-probability two-box patterns force that common value to zero. Thus \(C\succ0\). Diagonal normalization gives a symmetric positive-definite Z-matrix \(A=I-B\) with \(B\) strictly positive off diagonal and \(\rho(B)<1\); the Neumann series makes \(C^{-1}\) strictly positive. The exact-rational verifier checks formulas, principal minors, inverses, and direct small sample-space reconstructions.

evidence: Generic matrix theory covers the final inversion step after \(C\succ0\), but not the occupancy-specific threshold \(n=2\).

value.rationale: The exact rank transition and strict precision sign refine standard pairwise negative dependence for a canonical multinomial statistic and yield a clear structural statement about all full-order linear partial correlations.

final_claim: For iid sampling from finitely many positive-probability boxes, the occupied-box indicator covariance has rank \(m-1\) for one draw and is positive definite for every \(n\ge2\); for \(n\ge2\) its off-diagonal entries are strictly negative and its inverse is strictly positive entrywise, so all full-order linear partial correlations are negative.
limitations: Finite positive-probability category set and iid draws.
The precision statement is linear and second-order, not a nonlinear conditional-association theorem.
